sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s from accredited U.S. institution qualifies; at least six semesters completed for application
consideration, good standing in institutions attended. Mathematics committee evaluates holistically without a
department GPA cutoff. [s2] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare full PDF uploads before submitting; current central page says no document changes/additions
afterward. No faculty sponsor needed for admission or funding. [s2] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No faculty contact required to secure funding; faculty outside Graduate Committee do not decide
applications/funding. [s2]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Application portal; all intended materials before submission. Official records by 12 th class day. [s4]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Department rules standing; General Fellowship schedule explicitly 2027-28. [s7]

sections.text:
Academic application; Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
December 15 complete-file first-round review/full TA consideration; later rolling through spring. Standing date,
no year-specific department deadline. University January 15 fall priority is later than mathematics first round.

Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]

November 15, deadline February 3; awards March 21. [s1] [s7]
Accepting an offer [2027 confirmed]
General Fellowship 2027-28 award acceptance April 15. This does not establish all admission/TA offer
deadlines. [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL 79/Essentials 8.5, IELTS 6.5, PTE 60, DET 100; central older-scale TOEFL text should be
checked for 2026 scale. Most test validity 2 years; official agency records after admission. [s5]

UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed U.S. degree OR at least two consecutive years of U.S. university study in good standing exempts
English test; UChicago undergraduate meeting that duration qualifies. Teaching certification may be separate.
[s5] [s6]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
GRE not required. FAQ says submitted scores are not part of a complete application; no separate subject
requirement. Wording does not unequivocally say committee never considers optional scores. [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
TA starting stipend $2,000/month, increases at exam milestones; most tuition/fees remitted but student pays
some tuition each term. Paid months not specified, so annual total cannot be stated reliably. [s3]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
PhD support up to 5 years with good standing; sixth year request possible, not guaranteed. Positions
competitive, not automatic with admission. [s1] [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants included in common MS/PhD TA consideration; confirm teaching English clearance and
individual fellowship citizenship restrictions. [s1] [s5]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
TA automatic with admission application. Graduate School General Fellowships require separate
self-application and do not require admission first. [s1] [s7]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
General Fellowships typically $3,000-5,000/year. Recruitment fellowship $5,000/year up to 4 PhD years by
department nomination; DGSA $25,000/year plus tuition/fee waivers up to 4 years, also nominated.
Recruitment timetable published 2026-27, not yet 2027-28. [s7] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
International initial application $75, same-term subsequent application $25, credit card online; nonrefundable.
Old preview page adds late fee but current page does not: confirm if applying late. [s5]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Mathematics does not waive/pay application fees. Central international waiver limited to qualifying TTU-system
employees/spouse/dependents; no UChicago-F-1 hardship route verified. [s2] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Number theory and arithmetic geometry
Dermot McCarthy
Finite-field/p-adic hypergeometric functions, modular forms, point counts on hypersurfaces. [s10] [s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2024 · The number of F_q-points on diagonal hypersurfaces with monomial deformation
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Commutative and homological algebra
Lars Winther Christensen
Homological/homotopical methods in ring theory and singularity categories. [s10] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · The Improved New Intersection Theorem Revisited
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Algebra and number theory (adjacent)
Arne Ledet
Field theory, polynomials and associative algebras; recent paper not yet verified. [s10] [q14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2008; latest dated article on the author publication list · On generic differential SO_n-extensions
Historical evidence only. The official TTU profile links this author site; its indexed publication list was readable but live retrieval
timed out. No recent paper was established.
Number theory / computational algebra
Chris Monico
Computational algebra and number theory, algebraic cryptography, semigroup actions, invariants and
algorithms in the plactic monoid. [b15] [b15p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · Division in the plactic monoid
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Complex geometry / complex analysis
G. Brock Williams
Complex analysis and conformal or quasiconformal geometry; recent work studies holomorphic functions and
Bohr inequalities in complex Banach spaces. [b17] [b17p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · The Bohr-type inequalities for holomorphic functions with lacunary series in complex Banach space
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
